text:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding samples are inconsistent about which env var to use when customers have org/project-scoped API keys. Getting questions from integrators.

alex: Ugh yeah. Our Node quickstart just uses REDWOOD_API_KEY which breaks for teams that create project-scoped keys.

maya: Example from a user: 
```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_global_...
export REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY=sk_proj_abc123...
```
They expected the SDK to prefer REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY but it falls back to the global key.

sam: Proposed convention: SDKs should check in this order: 1) REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY 2) REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY 3) REDWOOD_API_KEY. Behavior: first non-empty wins. Make it explicit in samples.

chris: Strong +1. Also add a warning log if both project & global keys are set — easy footgun. Maybe only warn in dev mode.

maya: Agreed. Also need parity across languages (node/py/go/ruby). Right now only node has the fallback logic.

alex: I'll file a small RFC and make a PR that: updates samples, adds precedence logic to each SDK, and emits a single dev-only warning when both are present.

sam: Rotation question: how should SDKs handle rotating keys? We should recommend using short-lived session tokens when possible, but still support static keys. For rotation UX: support KEY_ID and KEY_AUTHSERVICE exchange flow in our guide.

maya: For docs: include recommended naming and examples for docker/k8s secrets (.env examples for different scopes). Also show how to set priority in k8s: project secret > global secret.

chris: Edge case: CLI and local dev. Recommend env var REDWOOD_API_KEY_LOCAL or REDWOOD_DEV_API_KEY? That feels messy. Maybe encourage use of profiles: REDWOOD_PROFILE=project-foo and a ~/.redwood/config with profile->key mapping. That avoids env var proliferation.

alex: Profiles seems reasonable but is more surface to implement. For now we should standardize the three env vars and doc the profile idea as next-step.

maya: UX bug to file: sample-apps/nextjs uses REDWOOD_API_KEY only — causes support tickets. I'll attach a failing repro.

devex-bot: linked issue: #4287 (auth/env-var-precedence) created by maya — https://go/redwood/4287

sam: Implementation detail: prefer explicit namespaced vars like REDWOOD_PROJECT_<PROJECT_ID>_API_KEY? That avoids ambiguity when multiple project keys in env, but it's more typing. Maybe only support REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY for sample apps and add advanced section for per-project vars.

chris: Also add a small helper util in each SDK: getApiKey({ projectId }) -> resolves precedence and returns which env var was used (for telemetry/diagnostics). Could return { key, source } so apps can log non-sensitive diagnostics.

maya: Love the helper idea. Helps onboarding. Also add a short snippet in quickstart:
```js
// node sample
const apiKey = process.env.REDWOOD_PROJECT_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_ORG_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey });
```

alex: I'll push the RFC + node + py changes first. @chris can you take go/ruby parity?

chris: Yep, will pick up go/ruby. Will also add warning flag and helper API.

maya: One more: rotation gotchas — recommend key metadata include creation_ts and last_used_ts surfaced in console, so ops can rotate safely. Add that to the doc checklist.

alex: Ok action items: create RFC, update samples, add SDK helper, doc rotation patterns, and file follow-up for profiles. I'll create PRs early next week. :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks — this should cut onboarding tickets by a lot. cc @sam @chris

sam: :thumbsup:

chris: :thumbsup:
